### Subject: Opinion on impact of fee-based vocational training receipts on charitable exemption under Sections 11/12

---

## 1. Purpose and Basis of this Opinion

This opinion is issued pursuant to our engagement letter dated [●], and is based solely on the facts and representations furnished by the management of Ananta Charitable Foundation, and on the relevant provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, applicable rules, notifications, circulars, and judicial precedents as they stand on the date hereof. We have not independently verified the facts provided to us. This opinion is addressed solely to, and for the sole use of, Ananta Charitable Foundation for the specific purpose stated herein, and should not be relied upon, quoted, or disclosed to any third party without our prior written consent.

## 2. Statement of Facts

Ananta Charitable Foundation, registered under Section 12AB, operates a vocational skill-training centre for underprivileged youth, charging a nominal fee that covers approximately 70% of operating costs, with the remainder funded through donations. Aggregate fee receipts for the year are INR 18 lakh.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

Whether the fee-based vocational training activity affects the Foundation's charitable status and exemption under Sections 11/12, having regard to the proviso to Section 2(15).

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 2(15)
- Section 11
- Section 12
- Section 12AB


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- ACIT (Exemptions) v. Ahmedabad Urban Development Authority, (2022) 449 ITR 1 (SC)

## 6. Analysis

Following the Supreme Court's ruling in Ahmedabad Urban Development Authority, vocational skill training for underprivileged youth falls within the distinct 'education' limb of Section 2(15) and is not subject to the 20% commercial-receipts proviso applicable to the residuary 'general public utility' category. As fees are charged at a level that merely covers, rather than exceeds, costs, and there is no profit motive, the activity does not amount to trade, commerce, or business.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

The Foundation's exemption under Sections 11/12 remains intact; the fee-based skill-training activity does not attract the general-public-utility commercial-receipts proviso under Section 2(15).

**Confidence level:** High
